title: A Microfluidic Technique to Probe Cell Deformability
protocol: Design the width of constriction array channels to be approximately 30-50% of the average cell diameter.
Ensure the channel height is at least 50% of the cell diameter for confinement in two dimensions.
Maintain a channel aspect ratio no less than 1:10 (height:width) throughout the device to prevent collapse.
Add support posts for channels exceeding the 1:10 aspect ratio, spacing them at least twice the cell diameter apart.
Include a filter at the entry ports to remove debris and disaggregate cell clusters.
Adjust the size and spacing of the filter posts so that the distance separating the posts is approximately equal to one cell diameter.
Fabricate the device master using standard techniques for lithographic micromachining.
Verify the height of the patterned features using a profilometer.
Set up an air supply tank and manual regulator.
Prepare the air source for pressure-driven flow, using a tank of compressed air and sequence of air regulators and fittings.
Set up an electronically controlled pressure regulator in-line with the manual regulator.
Use an electro-pneumatic converter to regulate and maintain a stable pressure drop across the channels, with pressure fluctuations of less than 2 kPa.
Write simple code in LabVIEW to input the desired pressure.
Set up a pressurized chamber to drive flow of the cell suspension.
Assemble a cell suspension chamber out of a standard flow cytometer tube and a machined cap that creates a pressure-tight seal on the tube.
Connect an inlet from the compressed air tank to the cell suspension chamber.
Connect an outlet through which cells flow from the pressurized chamber into the device.
Set up an inverted microscope fitted with a camera that has an acquisition rate of at least 100 frames per sec to capture images of the cells flowing through the constriction array.
Interface the camera with a video capture card and a computer.
Prepare a stock surfactant solution of 10% w/w Pluronic F-127 in phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Vortex and heat gently at 37°C to dissolve the F127.
Pass the solution through a 0.2 μm syringe filter.
Store the prepared surfactant solution at room temperature.
Mix PDMS thoroughly at a ratio of 1:10 (w/w) curing agent to base.
Pour the mixture over the device master.
Degas in a bell jar with applied vacuum until bubbles disappear, or for about 10-20 min.
Bake the degassed device at 65°C for 4 hr.
Remove microfluidic devices from the master mold.
Cut individual microfluidic devices out of the PDMS block with a razor blade.
Gently lift off one corner of the device to remove it from the master.
Punch holes in the PDMS device using a biopsy punch for connection ports.
Create holes from the channel side through to the exterior side of the device.
Rinse the PDMS device with isopropanol.
Direct a steady stream of pure isopropanol from a squeeze bottle through the holes in the PDMS device.
Blow dry the PDMS device with filtered air.
Place PDMS blocks with channels face up in a clean Petri dish.
Clean the glass substrate by rinsing with methanol.
Blow dry the glass substrate with filtered air.
Place the glass substrate on a 200 °C hotplate for 5-10 min.
Oxygen plasma treat the channel side of the PDMS block.
Oxygen plasma treat one side of a glass slide.
Place the channel side of the PDMS on top of the treated side of the glass immediately after treatment.
Hold together with light pressure for ~10 sec to promote bonding.
Bake the entire device at an elevated temperature (60-80 °C) for at least 15 min.
Inspect the microfluidic device under a microscope.
Ensure that the channels are not collapsed or broken and that both inlet and outlet holes connect directly into the device channels by using a low-power objective (10X).
Designate defective devices by scoring the surface of the PDMS with a razor blade and do not use them for experiments.
Culture HL-60 cells in RPMI-1640 medium supplemented with 1% penicillin-streptomycin solution and 10% fetal bovine serum in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37 °C.
Harvest adherent cells by trypsinization.
Add ~0.5 ml of trypsin to a flask with a 25 cm² culture area.
Resuspend the cells in ~30 ml of fresh medium.
Differentiate HL-60 cells into neutrophil-type cells using all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) at a final concentration of 5 µM per 1 x 10⁵ cells/ml.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 x g for 3 min.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant and resuspend cells to the appropriate final density in fresh culture medium with 0.1% v/v F-127.
Count the cells using a Coulter counter, hemacytometer, or flow cytometer.
Adjust the cell suspension to a density of 1 x 10⁶ to 5 x 10⁶ cells/ml.
Supplement the cell suspension with approximately 0.1% v/v F-127.
Place cell suspension in a flow cytometer tube and connect to the pressure cap.
Adjust the pressure to about 14-21 kPa and flush until the cell suspension emerges from the tubing tip.
Insert the tip of the tubing containing the cell suspension into the device inlet.
Route a piece of tubing into an empty tube for waste collection taped to the side of the microscope stage.
Ensure that the inlet and outlet tubing is of the same diameter and approximately the same length for each experiment.
Gently ramp up the pressure to about 28 kPa or until cells flow through the channels.
Position the device so that multiple channels are in the field of view and perpendicular to the bottom of the screen.
Acquire multiple videos if the camera is limited by data size to generate sufficient independent data points.
Adjust the frame rate as necessary for desired data output.
Use high speed imaging at 300 frames per second to capture changes in cell shape.
Use a frame rate of approximately 100 fps to measure transit times of cells.
Open the file Master_script.m and run the program.
Select the first video to be analyzed from the Windows Explorer window that appears.
Specify the frame rate for the selected video and press enter.
Select a rectangular cropping window in the figure that encompasses all channels left to right.
Ensure the cropping window intersects the channels just above the first bulb of the array at top and bottom.
Select constriction regions from the cropped image.
Maintain a fixed pixel distance between the top and bottom window boundary for every video selected.
Monitor the top left image closely to determine if the algorithm is accurately locating cells.
Select the next video to be processed from the Windows Explorer window.
Repeat steps 5.2-5.5 for each video selected.
Select cancel once all desired videos have been added via the Windows Explorer window.
The algorithm will perform remaining operations without user intervention.
Upon completion, the algorithm will produce a histogram of the transit time data.
Save the data in the directory as a MATLAB .mat file and a Microsoft Excel .xls file.
